title: The effect of pressure on the splitting in $^3$He in nematic aerogel
authors: V. V. Dmitriev, D. V. Petrova, A. A. Soldatov, A. N. Yudin
abstract: Here, we present the results of an investigation of how the pressure affects the splitting of the superfluid transition temperature in $^3$He in anisotropic aerogel. It is well known that boundary conditions significantly influence the properties of superfluid phases in aerogel. When aerogel strands are coated with a $^4$He layer in magnetic field, new phases, such as the polar, polar-distorted A (DA), polar-distorted B (DB), and $β$ phases, become energetically favorable. In contrast, without this coating, the system tends to favor phases resembling the bulk A, B, and A$_1$ phases. Our earlier results showed a nonlinear dependence of the superfluid transition temperature splitting in pure $^3$He, but the range of nonlinearity did not match the theoretical predictions based on magnetic scattering effects. To further investigate this discrepancy, we performed measurements of the splitting under varying pressures for both pure $^3$He and with $^4$He coverage of the aerogel strands.
summary: The research investigates how pressure influences the superfluid transition temperature splitting of $^3$He confined in nematic aerogels. By comparing results from samples coated with $	ext{}^4	ext{He}$ versus pure $^3$He, the authors test theoretical models describing boundary effects. The findings suggest that coating the pores leads to a more theoretically consistent description of the phase transitions under pressure.
main_problem: The study investigates how external pressure affects the splitting of the superfluid transition temperature ($T_c$) in $^3$He confined within anisotropic nematic aerogels.
main_result: The presence of a $	ext{}^4	ext{He}$ coating on the aerogel strands leads to a more symmetric field dependence for the transition splitting, which shows better agreement with theoretical predictions at higher applied pressures compared to pure $^3$He samples.
method: Measurements were performed using a vibrating wire (VW) resonator and quartz tuning fork for thermometry while applying varying magnetic fields and pressures. Transition temperatures were determined by analyzing resonance frequency and Full Width at Half-Maximum (FWHM).
model_or_system: The system is superfluid $^3$He confined in nematic aerogels, comparing boundary conditions: specular reflection (with $	ext{}^4	ext{He}$ coating) versus diffuse scattering/impurity effects (pure $^3$He). Theoretical models include Ginzburg-Landau coefficients and impurity magnetization descriptions.
key_observables: Superfluid transition temperature splitting ($\Delta T$), resonance frequency, Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM), and the ratio of slopes of the transitions with respect to magnetic field ($H$).
important_parameters: Applied pressure (e.g., 7.1 bar, 15.4 bar, 19.4 bar) and applied magnetic field ($H$ up to $31 	ext{ kOe}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between boundary scattering mechanisms ($	ext{}^4	ext{He}$ coating vs. pure $	ext{}^3	ext{He}$) and compares observed nonlinearities against established theoretical models.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of FWHM and resonance frequency for both coated and uncoated samples at various pressures, highlighting the distinct transition regimes ($T_{ca1}, T_{ca2}$ vs. $T_{P1}, T_{P2}$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares experimental results under varying pressure and boundary conditions ($	ext{}^4	ext{He}$ coating vs. pure $	ext{}^3	ext{He}$) to resolve discrepancies between previous measurements and theoretical predictions regarding $T_c$ splitting.
why_interesting: This work bridges condensed matter physics (superfluidity, phase transitions) with materials science (porous media confinement), providing experimental validation for complex boundary condition effects on quantum fluid behavior.
